stem_en: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. $\mathrm{HCl}$ + $\mathrm{ZnCl2}$, known as Lucas Reagent. Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

statements.label: I
statements.text: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. $\mathrm{HCl}$ + $\mathrm{ZnCl2}$, known as Lucas Reagent.

statements.label: II
statements.text: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent.

options_en.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options_en.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options_en.3: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options_en.4: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

b6_reason: Lucas reagent is indeed conc. HCl with anhydrous ZnCl2 used to distinguish the three classes, but tertiary alcohols (not primary) give immediate turbidity, so Statement II is wrong.
